summary: The study investigates the effects of initial growth mode on the electrical properties of HfO2 films deposited via atomic layer deposition (ALD) on different starting surfaces. The results show that wet chemical oxide surfaces lead to more layer-like growth and better electrical properties compared to thermal oxide surfaces. The process uses HfCl4 and H2O as precursors, and the growth mechanism involves preferential reaction with Si-OH sites.
evidence: The effects of the initial growth mode on the electrical properties of atomic-layer-deposited HfO2 films were investigated. HfO2 films were deposited on various Si surfaces by a showerhead-type ALD at a temperature of 300°C. The precursors used for the Hf source and the O source were HfCl4 and H2O, respectively. The study showed that wet chemical oxide surfaces led to more layer-like growth and better electrical properties compared to thermal oxide surfaces.
